How it works

Your rank comes from your best valid card. Each game on the card contributes its score multiplied by that machine's multiplier.

The numbers below are examples, not tournament results.

1. Calculate each game's points

Multipliers balance scores between machines. For example, a score of 280,000 on Stars is worth 140,000,000 points.

Stars score280,000×Multiplier500=Points140,000,000
See machine multipliers →

2. Add the points for one card

This example has two games from each era. Add their adjusted points to get the card total.

Machine / raw score × multiplierAdjusted points
StarsOld280,000 × 500
140,000,000
QuicksilverOld340,000 × 150
51,000,000
CreatureMid120,000,000 × 0.8
96,000,000
TheatreMid700,000,000 × 0.12
84,000,000
Iron MaidenNew360,000,000 × 0.33
118,800,000
Jurassic ParkNew120,000,000 × 0.35
42,000,000
Card total531,800,000

3. Use the best valid card

If one player submits these three cards, Card B is the one that counts.

Card AValid · lower total
441,800,000
Card BBest valid card · counts for standings
531,800,000
Card CInvalid · three Mid-era games
606,800,000

Card C has the highest total, but it exceeds the limit of 2 games per era. It stays in the player's history and is excluded from the standings.

Games from different cards aren't combined. A better game on Card A doesn't replace a game on Card B.

If a score or card looks wrong, ask a tournament director.
